correctness.rationale: Inspected frozen RESULT.md SHA 4779918cb6fbf978d8239d4f445e00972b32ce0b and verify.py SHA bd2831ec18767ad478e1279b3d7d20642f63a9ed. For n≥2, Fourier inverse of −i sgn(k)(1−|k|/n), with DC/Nyquist zero, is Q_n(r)=2Σ_{k=1}^{n−1}(1−k/n) sin(πkr/n). Finite geometric derivative gives [sin t−n^-1 sin(nt)]/(1−cos t). Critical grid t=πr/n kills sin(nt); Q= cot(πr/2n) except original sine-sum zero at r=0,n. Normalized circulant row L1 mass and sign-vector/point-mass witnesses prove both endpoint ℓ¹/ℓ∞ norms C_n=(1/n)Σ_{r=1}^{n−1}cot(πr/2n). Partition even and odd terms in C_(2n) to derive 2C_(2n)−C_n=(1/n)Σ_{j=0}^{n−1}cot((2j+1)π/(4n))=untapered cyclic Hilbert L_(4n). Subtract (2/πx) singularity from cot(πx/2) and apply Euler–Maclaurin with H_(n−1) to yield (2/π)log n+(2/π)(γ+log(2/π))−π/(36n²)+O(n^-4). Separately recomputed exact cot sum vs direct multiplier for representative n and high-precision n² residual near −π/36; numerical tests corroborate, not prove, infinite claims.
